blocking.item: 'Maker-held' nets whose governing edge is a bound: w5si-record.md sections 5.1, 5.2 and Q4/Q5; drafts/w5si/readings/bound_decides.txt; the PARA in apply_coverage_si001.py; ER-D12 in pcb_edge_rates.yaml
blocking.problem:
By the tool's own table, 40 of the 83 'maker-held' nets have a BOUND as their fastest candidate (0.000 ns), and their critical length in the table is 0.0 mm. The records describe these nets by the maker's figure instead. Where they are:
- Board A: SCL, SDA, EXP_INT, PROCHOT.
- Board B: SCL, SDA, EXP_INT, HB1 to HB3, BBM1/2/3 and their _ARMR, _MOV and _REQ nets, BSEL1 to BSEL3, and the SWCLK and SWDIO lines of all three controllers.
- Board C: SCL, SDA, EXP_INT, HB1 to HB3.
- Board D: SCL, SDA, EXP_INT.

The bounds that govern them come from BQ25731, KSZ9897, RP2040, Nexperia 74LVC1G157, Diodes 74LVC1G17, a discrete FET drain, and the bench probe.

What the records say instead:
- bound_decides.txt, which is to be filed as a record, prints for example 'MAKER SCL at 0.451 ns (critical 10.5 mm)' for board A's SCL. The reading's own evidence line is 'LAYOUT_BOUND SCL (CLOCKED_DIGITAL, 0.000 ns BOUND TI-BQ25731, critical 0.0 mm)'.
- The coverage paragraph that would be committed to the registry says the kit I2C bus and EXP_INT are held by the STM32H743 at 0.45 ns and the PCA9555 INT at 0.12 ns. It gives board B's voter and supervisor lines critical lengths of 2.6 to 10.5 mm.
- ER-D12 justifies the split as 'the bound changes a number in the table and no outcome'. But the module's own docstring says that number is the length handed to layout, so the bound does decide an outcome.
- Q4 and Q5 propose remedies (slow the STM32, series resistors at the LVC or ADS1115 outputs). These do not close the 40 nets, because the unmodelled drivers stay on them.

Fix: count the mixed nets as their own category, or under BOUND_DECIDES for the length. State their critical length as the bound's. Name the bound drivers in 5.1, 5.2, Q4, Q5, the readings file and the coverage PARA, and correct ER-D12's reason.

Evidence: /tmp/<scratchpad>/chk-w5si/evidence_maker_held_bound_governed.txt, re-derived from my own run of edge_length.py on the c23c5e76 netlists, which reproduces the author's counts exactly.

blocking.item: drafts/w5si/apply_board_b_declarations.py: G_OLD and G_NEW, the change to gen_pcb_b3.py PATTERNS
blocking.problem:
G_OLD is only a prefix of line 573. G_NEW appends a '# ...' comment in the middle of that line, so the rest of the line becomes comment text. That silently deletes four USB pair-class patterns: ('GNSS_D*','USB'), ('ZBA_D*','USB'), ('ZBB_D*','USB') and ('RB_D*','USB'). PATTERNS goes from 40 entries to 37.

The result still parses, and assert g2 != g still holds, so the draft's own checks pass. At board B's next layout generation, GNSS_DM/DP, ZBA_DM/DP, ZBB_DM/DP and RB_DM/DP would lose the USB class and its impedance target. This is a weakened protection hidden in a draft.

Reproduced by applying the draft to a scratch copy of c23c5e76 and to an extract of fnd/r8int6 at 932cf9d7; evidence in /tmp/<scratchpad>/chk-w5si/evidence_gen_pcb_b3_after_draft.diff.

Fix: put the comment on its own line, or replace only the tuples. Also assert that the evaluated PATTERNS list keeps every pattern except the four intended changes.

blocking.item: W5SI-D2 in apply_board_b_declarations.py: board B's BOB reclassified from CLOCKED_DIGITAL to LOW_SPEED_OR_DC
blocking.problem:
The identification is right: BOB is the Bob Smith termination, R9 and R10 at 75 ohm to C33, 1 nF 2 kV (gen_sch_b.py:1151). The chosen class is not.

LOW_SPEED_OR_DC is exactly the class that return_via.py:177 and ref_change.py:127 skip ('slow += 1; continue'). The signal_class.py definition is 'There is no edge to speak of'. This node exists to carry the Ethernet common-mode current to ground, so its return path is part of its job. The draft therefore removes BOB from two EMC return rules while its basis says 'its layout belongs to the magnetics and the EMC rules', and it does not disclose that effect. That narrows the scope of those checks to settle an SI-001 UNDECIDED.

Fix: keep a class that asks the ADJACENT question, for example HIGH_SPEED_DIGITAL with the corrected Bob Smith basis. Answer SI-001 for BOB separately, with a BOUND interface record covering b: ['BOB'] plus an edge_allow declaration naming what holds its length, or leave it UNDECIDED and named.

minor: The author's summary says '753 of the 765 nets that had no decided edge are now decided'. That is wrong. 753 is the total decided after the change, out of 829 non-slow signal nets. Of the 765 nets that were undecided before, 689 are now decided and 76 remain (75 carry no class declaration, plus BOB). The per-board numbers in the record and in the coverage draft are correct.

ER-D10's reason is wrong. It says HW-FW-CONTRACT.md records no obligation that holds any of these pins slow, but two rows do:
- FW-K02 holds the panel RP2040's GPIO0/1 (the kit I2C) at the default 4 mA drive and slow slew.
- FW-B08 limits the STM32's PB6/PB7 to I2C1 target duty.

No figure changes, because the RP2040 publishes no edge at either slew setting. The header should cite both rows. Also, FW-K02 claims the kit bus fall stays above the specification's floor, which the new IBIS figures (STM32 at 0.451 ns, ADS1115 SDA_HS at 0.786 ns) put in question. That belongs in Q5.

Families with no `inputs` regex count input pins as bound-0 drivers. BQ25731 pin 13 SCL is 'I' in TI's pin table, and KSZ9897 SCL_MDC is an input in I2C target mode. Board A's SCL evidence therefore names an input pin as the net's fastest driver. The error is on the pessimistic side, but it is still an instrument defect in the attribution. Add the inputs.

ibis_read.py fails open in two ways:
- A model with no parsed Model_type is read as INPUT.
- A '[Model_Selector]' keyword spelled with an underscore is missed.

It should return UNKNOWN in both cases. This has no effect on the 13 files held today: every model in them is typed and all use '[Model Selector]'.

Other silent limits of the resolver. None has any effect on today's netlists; all such nets are bound-0 or in a slow class. Each should become a reason, or at least be stated:
- A passive switch pin that is neither a through pin nor a declared input is dropped without a reason.
- SKY13351's through regex '^SW' matches pin functions that are really net names, so a net rename in the r8int6 regeneration would drop the far side silently.
- Relay K1, the SW_* switches and T1 are never asked.
- On a continued board (no_far), a connector leading off the set contributes nothing and gives no reason.

Only 6 of the 13 IBIS families check the supply rail. The 7 without the check are TI-INA226, TI-TMP117, TI-TCAN334, TI-SN74LVC1G57, TI-ADS1115, TI-TUSB8041 and ST-STM32H743. I verified all of them are at 3.3 V today:
- INA226 VS on +3V3.
- TMP117 on +3V3_DEV.
- TCAN334 on +3V3_IOCA.
- LVC1G57 on +3V3.
- ADS1115 on +3V3.
- STM32 VDD on +3V3_IOCA.

A later change of rail would not be caught.
The rules_status CONFIG_INPUTS draft names the other boards' netlists by phase-specific path (pcb-a-power-a23, and so on). The entry has to be re-derived whenever a board's declared phase moves.

Sessions decisions ER-D1 to ER-D12, W5SI-D1 and W5SI-D2 are recorded only in the data file header and the draft docstrings. ER-D8, ER-D9 and ER-D12 change what SI-001 counts as decided. Consider rows in pcb_decisions.yaml (authority SESSION, authority_why, reversed_by), under the owner's 21 September rule.

The coverage draft moves SI-001's remediation from LAB/HARDWARE to SESSION/PARALLEL_AGENT. That holds only where a termination or an impedance target answers the net. Any bound-governed net answered by a declared length still needs a maker model or a measurement at bring-up. Also, 'Raspberry Pi's IBIS model on request' is outside contact, which stays with the owner; prepare the text only.

Many BOUND records' `checked` quotes are just the part name ('SA868', 'HDMI', 'SIM', '9704', 'SUNON'). That proves the document is held, not that anyone searched it for a transition time. My spot check of 11 datasheets found no missed published minimum: RP2040, CP2102N, ATECC608B, BMI270, SGP41, BME688, BQ25731, BQ4050, W25Q16JV, TUSB2046B and VEML7700.

LVC1G34-BUFFER's verification_owed points to TI's SN74LVC1G34 model. But SOURCES.yaml (logic-held-sheets-round-8, C526347) pins U506 to Diodes 74LVC1G34W5-7, and board D's U18 to U20 use the same code. The replacement model has to be Diodes' model.

The IBIS records say 'none for the number' under verification_owed, while ER-D5 itself says a later die is a question for the maker. Make the two consistent: the TI files were re-fetched today and are TI's current models.

Q8: TI's IBIS headers prohibit redistribution, and the integration pushes to the public GitHub mirror. The record says publication is the owner's. The integrator should either rely explicitly on the owner's standing v2/vendor ruling (published as-is, takedown on request) or hold the .ibs files out of the commit.

What I confirmed (no action needed):
- IBIS figures: I re-derived all 13 with my own parser; every one matches, per pin. LVC08A 0.215, LVC32A 0.136, LVC86A 0.113, 1G00 0.282, 1G04 0.198, 1G57 0.221, PCA9555 INT 0.121 / ports 5.89 / SDA 72.3, TCAN334 RXD 1.5694, INA226 16.0634, TMP117 7.6757, ADS1115 SDA_HS 0.7865, TUSB8041 0.0057, STM32 io8_ft_hs_3v3 0.451 typ fall (max corner 0.563), ls 6.70, i2c 8.83.
- ER-D11 is justified: at 1.8 V the hslv and ft hs pads agree within 7 percent, and the ft pad is the faster one.
- Published minimums confirmed in the makers' PDFs: TPS25740 CC 300 ns and digital output fall 20 ps (70 to 30 percent), TPS23861 SDAO 21 ns, DS3231 20+0.1Cb, PI7C9X2G404SL 175 ps. DS12110 Table 53 gives maxima only (1.5 ns at 10 pF).
- Identity: I re-fetched TI SCEM292, SLLM313, SCEM010, SCPM035 and SBOM458 from ti.com and their sha256 are identical to the held files. The SOURCES draft shas match. The PCA9555 resolves to TI PCA9555PWR. TCAN334 D and DCN pins are identical (SLLSEQ7F Table 4-1). No merge of parts with differing ratings carries a real figure.
- Readings: before and after both reproduced on the c23c5e76 netlists (A 6/114/0 to 82/38/63, B 30/532/0 to 553/9/193, C 4/33/0 to 33/4/23, D 20/27/2 to 39/8/13, E 4/37/0 to 41/0/31, P 0/22/0 to 5/17/1; all INCONCLUSIVE).
- Tests: test_edge_length 28 passed. With all four drafts applied, 138 of 139 passed in the affected set; the one failure was my scratch copy lacking the v2/release link and passed once it was linked.
- All four drafts apply on the current fnd/r8int6 head 932cf9d7, which is no longer the 053a0524 the author used, and SI-001 there reads the same counts.
- Nothing was edited in the worktree or the main checkout.
